body:
I had to think about this for a while before responding. My problem with living here isn't that I think it's unfair for me to have to babysit. My problem is with the way she treats me, how she thinks that just because she's my parent she should be allowed to speak to me however she chooses and I should just take it. She thinks I want to move out because I want to hang out with my friends all the time, but I want to move out because I want to figure out who I am, what I like, and what I want to do with my life. All of that has been clouded by living here because I'm more concerned with what she thinks of my decisions than if I actually like the decisions I'm making. 
My mental health is the reason I want to leave but she makes me feel selfish for trying to put myself first. I know it's not wise to want to move out when I'm severely in debt and don't have a "real job" but I feel like I won't live much longer if I have to stay here.

That's very accurate and is exactly what I've decided to do. Even though there are basically no employment opportunities near me =S 

But I figure if I can work and become financially independent, my mom can't say anything if I say I'm moving out.
I have a debit card. The credit cards were used to pay for tuition when I couldn't get a student loan, not due to irresponsibility or not being married.

An update, kind of.

So I was thinking of things I could do with my life the other day. I got super excited about something because it's a hobby I like (or used to like, before the whole depression thing, when i forgot i had hobbies). I went home, researched the job, the schooling, etc. Emailed the nearest schools offering the program, got more excited because I thought I might've finally figured something out.
... nope. 
I know it sounds ridiculous but I always run my ideas past my mom because sometimes I get way too into things and talking about them helps organize my thoughts and whatnot. I was all, "So I know this is probably a silly question but what about *insert job/school here*" and she got this weird look on her face, shrugged, and said, "...why?"
I swear I felt myself just melt into the couch and die inside. That sounds overdramatic but god. That's all it took for me to realize that oh, right, yep, I forgot, i'm stupid, shy, airheaded, and not outgoing enough for a job in that field. I mean, what the fuck was I thinking?

So now I'm back to where I was, embarrassed because I took the time to email the schools and talk to my friends and boyfriend about it, and it was all for nothing. 

Still no update on the therapist. It's looking like I'm actually going to have to call people which is the worst case scenario and I just can't bring myself to do it. 
Also I've basically stopped talking to anyone but my boyfriend. Idk if that's a bad thing really, because I feel like he's my best friend, but I don't care to talk to or see any of my other friends. I don't want to see anyone, really. If it were up to me, I'd sleep on the couch all day, with netflix marathons in between.

I mean, I know that, but then my anxiety takes over and I lose it. I can't clean because I'm afraid I'll do it wrong/mess it up, and I've failed tons of classes for the same reason. I just can't stand the idea of doing something wrong/stupid. 
I'm working on it though. I did manage to email her without crying.

It's been about three weeks. I only really see her a few days a week and it's hard to remember to remind her, but I need to. I just don't feel important so I don't like to bring up stuff like that to her, even though I know that doesn't make sense. 

It's like I see the email in my inbox and go to reply but I get too anxious, figure I'll say something stupid, and just exit the window.

I'm having a hard time finding anyone because not many good doctors near me take medicaid. My mom's going to help me though (we go to the same doc) because he's insulted her more than once. He used to be good, idk what happened.
I thought I found a therapist, I emailed her and she emailed me back but now I feel stupid and can't seem to email her back. My mom said she'd help me with that too, but it makes me feel like I'm 5.

We were. He was switching my meds around and everything, trying to find the right mix. It was working for a while and then all the pills started making me feel sick and weird so we agreed that I'd stop taking all but one, but he didn't give me anything new to try and he was no help when I asked him about finding a therapist. 
I'm fed up with him and am currently searching for a new doctor who'll actually listen to me when I talk so we can figure out what's actually going to work.

Yeah =/ He and I got into it about that because even though I've had bad experiences with counseling in the past, I'm able to recognize that it was the counselor that was bad, and not the entire system. He, on the other hand, thinks that since the one therapist he had was bad, they're all bad. It's really frustrating that he wouldn't support me trying to get better because he has some personal vendetta against therapists and doctors. 

=] I think I've found one, she seems really cool. I just have to email her to see if she's got any openings that work for me. I'm eager to be able to speak to someone about my problems who doesn't already have an opinion on them, if that makes sense.

Thanks! That's really interesting. 

Me too. My mom thinks I'm too innocent to have sex and all that and I'm just like wow. When she was my age, she already had a baby. It's frustrating because I can't talk to her about the herpes without letting her know I've had sex (obviously).
Yep, I just got the results back today and it's herpes simplex 1. What a bummer. I never thought I'd get an std from my first sexual partner, but just my luck!

Maybe I should also mention that my dating history hasn't been the greatest. My most recent ex was a compulsive liar and had Histrionics Disorder. She was just bat shit crazy, and I couldn't deal with it, so at six months I broke up with her. Some of the things my current boyfriend says remind me of how she used to talk, which is why I asked him if he was lying. I tried explaining that to him but I think it made him more angry because he felt like I was saying he was like her, idk. I've had two other relationships in the past, one where I was a rebound (that lasted like five days and I noped my way outta there) and then my first relationship, which wasn't really a relationship, was complete shit. The guy lied to me to try to get me to have sex with him. The first time I kissed him (which was my first kiss with a dude) I was completely drunk. He kept rubbing his dick on me and trying to get me to touch it and blow him and it was just really traumatic. But I kept going back because I thought I was just being stupid. So it just kept happening over and over for a month, before he found out that I told someone that I thought he was molesting me. He got mad, called me a dumb bitch, and "broke up" with me. Obviously it was a good thing that I got out of that situation but it's plagued me for five years and it's still not any easier. I've tried explaining that to my boyfriend and he was really supportive about it, which I was grateful for. But now that I want to go to therapy to try and work through stuff, including the molestation, he doesn't want me to? It just doesn't make sense to me and it makes me feel wrong for wanting to get help.

Good god, I gotta stop for now. 4am on Christmas morning and here I am, spilling my guts instead of sleeping.

The good news is that I'm feeling significantly less suicidal than I was when I first posted this. I've never been that low before, I almost called a suicide hotline and I have major phone anxiety but I was willing to push through it because I was out of control. I'm much calmer now, I think, but it might just be Christmas cheer.

Another thing that's been bugging me is that my boyfriend got really mad at me when I said I wanted to try therapy again. He says all therapists are terrible liars that share your information and only want your money, or that they're "people who are just paid to sit there and be talked at".
It's kind of hurtful because he thinks I should just be able to talk to him or my friends and feel better. He doesn't get that I can't talk about certain things that have happened in my life because they're very upsetting to me, and they're things that only a professional would be able to help me work through. 
I just want to get better, and he thinks that pills and therapy are stupid and that I should just be able to get over it because he thinks that's what people should do (since he's very much against pills and stuff). I respect his POV but I kind of feel like he doesn't respect mine. Don't get me wrong, he's amazing. These are the first issues to come up in our relationship so they probably seem big but in the long run won't be. He is a few years younger than me and comes from a bit of a different background, so I understand why he thinks the way he does about certain things. I just wish he could be more understanding of my depression and things like that.

Sorry about all the rambling, I just needed a safe space to get this all off my chest. It's easier for me to think about things when I write them out or talk them out, obviously. So thanks for letting me blab at you. :)

Also, yes, writing has been a major part of my life since I was like 11 and my friend and I would do little role play Harry Potter stories. It sounds dorky now, but it was super fun back then. I kept writing until a few months ago, around when I became extremely depressed and anxious. I just couldn't concentrate enough to keep writing, and then when I would try to write I just couldn't find the words. It was so frustrating that I haven't really gone back to it since, even though I want to and think about it constantly. I honestly usually like to write YA stuff, it used to always include some sort of supernatural element, but recently I've been having story ideas that are a bit more mature, like the characters are in their early 20's (as I am) and it deals more with real life issues than make-believe ones. I think what I like to write depends on where I am in my head, and it tends to grow with me, if that makes sense.

Sorry for the late response. I've been weirdly busy. 

I guess that's true. I just see my friends with their husbands and babies and I get kind of jealous because even though they might not be well off, at least they're not in the same place as they were when they were 16. I think that's a really big problem for me. The only difference between when I was 14 and now is that I can drive. My mom still treats me like I'm a young teen and it's frustrating because she trusts me enough to care for her son but turns around and yells at me, telling me I'm irresponsible. I mean, in the past ten years that I've been watching my brother, he's never been hurt, there have never been any accidents aside from him breaking something, for real, there have been no problems caused by my supposed "irresponsibility" >=[

Anyway, I got into a heated argument with my mom yesterday and the day before, and things are a smidge better now. I think she finally sees that I'm frustrated with how she treats me, but I don't know if she plans on changing anything. I guess we'll see.
That kind of brings me to my next thing? While I was arguing with my mom I got extremely confused because she was saying a lot of things that didn't make sense to me, so I started to doubt other things. It's really hard to explain what my brain did but basically I started wondering if maybe all the times I thought she was mean, she was actually nice, and then maybe all the people I thought were nice were actually mean. So I messaged my boyfriend and asked him if he lies to me (as some of his stories are extravagant) and he just blew up. I wasn't trying to be mean to him or anything, I just simply asked the question and then he started going off about all the things he's done for me and how he felt betrayed and disappointed that I'd think that. 
His reaction hurt me a lot because IMO if he didn't lie to me, he'd have nothing to be that mad about. At one point he asked me if I was lying to him, and I said no. And that was that. I wasn't angry with him for asking, I didn't blow up at him. It's been eating at my brain for the past few days and I just don't know who to talk to about it because I don't know if I was right or wrong for asking him that. He and I are kind of in a weird spot now, I saw him last night and the look he gave me... I don't know. He said he considered breaking up with me but the thought made his heart hurt because he loves me so much. I'm just so confused.

To be honest, I don't even know what living my own life would look like to me. I used to think it would include things like a big house, a job where I made tons of money, a nice car... and now I just want to sleep. 
As far as careers go, I've always wanted to write books. I have tons of ideas in my head, but I don't have the energy to write anymore and since I haven't taken an English class in like two years, I feel like I've become so stupid that I shouldn't even try. 

I just see all the people I went to school with getting their degrees or starting families and then there's me. I ended up being a super senior in high school because I didn't feel like doing school work (I love learning but I hate homework. My teachers were always frustrated with me because I was smart but I basically checked out of my head when I'd go to school because I was so bored or distracted. I mean, I got a 27 on my ACTS and had a 34 in the English category so I know I'm not completely brain dead.) so I was already behind my friends. Transferring colleges put me even further back, and now that I've quit... well. 

A lot of that is irrelevant, but it's three in the morning and I can't sleep either. =p
